title: Each execution and each gate runs in a resource envelope of its own: a systemd user scope in Spawn's slice, limits that hold, a memory-limit kill that ends that execution only and is resumed, a gate its envelope kills judged again as a host fault, and admission that waits for room
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs, the module comment, `launch` and `Launch` (the pane runs `spawn run -- <engine>` with the environment it is given), how an execution ends (`exit_status`; the `is_alive` check that calls a vanished terminal `Lost`; `end`: the final checkpoint, the kill, the unmount, then `execution.ended`), `recover` and `catch_up` (a restarted Bridge carries on with the engines still running), and `EndCause` in crates/spawn-core/src/event.rs; crates/spawn-cli/src/commands/engine.rs (`run`: the runner waits for the engine and writes SPAWN_EXIT_FILE); `start` in crates/spawn-host/src/tmux.rs (`new-session`: tmux 3.8 on this host moves every pane into a scope of its own, app.slice/tmux-spawn-<uuid>.scope, which is tmux's, not Spawn's); crates/spawn-cli/src/runtime.rs (the Bridge's configuration from the environment); `resident_loop` in crates/spawn-cli/src/commands/loops.rs; crates/spawn-cli/src/disk.rs (the floor under which no execution starts, `hold_new_executions`, and the `host.disk` record read back on start: the pattern for `host.envelope`); `decide` and `keep_residents` in crates/spawn-cli/src/supervise.rs and `resume_lost` in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch/worker.rs; in crates/spawn-cli/src/gate.rs how the gate process is started (`Command::new("sh")`, its process group, the kill at the wall clock, `GATE_ENV`) and in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs the judging thread that runs it; crates/spawn-postgres/src/host.rs and `spawn_host_record` in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (it accepts `host.disk` only); deploy/systemd/spawn-loop.service and spawn-integrate.service (KillMode=process: a loop restart leaves the engines running), deploy/systemd/README.md and deploy/deploy.sh; rsi/backlog/018.json (the resource checks before a gate: this objective generalises its memory check from gates to executions), rsi/backlog/020.json (the verdict `host_fault`, its backoff, its run and its escalation: a gate its envelope kills is one) and rsi/backlog/028.json (`execution.interrupted`, cause `memory_limit`, path `resume`: how the kill is recorded and recovered); the header of scripts/rsi/gate.sh on the sandbox (/run is empty: no user manager is reachable inside it); docs/design.md §11 and §14, docs/storage.md ("Disk room"); `man systemd.resource-control` (MemoryHigh, MemoryMax, MemorySwapMax, CPUWeight, OOMPolicy) and `man systemd-run` (--scope, --slice, --unit, --collect, -p).

The problem. Spawn's executions have no envelope. On 2026-11-06 at 16:30 CST (08:30 UTC) this host (16 CPUs, 31.3 GiB of RAM, 31.3 GiB of swap on zram, which is compressed RAM) ran 11 live Spawn engines, each in the scope tmux makes for its pane (app.slice/tmux-spawn-<uuid>.scope) with memory.max and memory.swap.max `max` and the CPU weight of every other job of the user (100). Their anonymous memory then: 69-271 MB each, 1.8 GB together; their memory.peak (page cache included): 0.28-4.7 GB. The integrator's service, which runs the gates, peaked at 5.3 GB over two full gates (16:31-16:54 CST, 08:31-08:54 UTC, tasks 91 and 93; 173 MB of it in swap); the owner's own panes (builds and gates run by hand) peaked at 8.6-25.2 GB. Nothing bounds an execution: one build, test or tool that runs away takes the host's memory and then its swap, and every execution and gate on the host, Spawn's or not, slows or is killed with it, by the kernel's choice; Spawn's work also competes with the host's other jobs at an equal CPU weight (at 14:43 CST (06:43 UTC) that day a gate's setup took 244 s instead of 28 on a loaded host).

The user manager can do it without root, verified on this host on 2026-11-06 (systemd 262): user@1000.service has the controllers cpuset cpu io memory pids and enables cpu memory pids for its units. `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=64M -p MemorySwapMax=0 python3 ...` allocating 320 MB was killed in 130 ms (exit 137, "Failed with result 'oom-kill'"); in a 96M scope a second process of the scope was killed with the allocating one (a scope's default OOMPolicy=stop), the slice above it counted the kill (its memory.events oom_kill 1: hierarchical; memory.events.local 0), and with --collect no unit stayed behind. A cap without a swap cap is no cap here: the same 64M scope without MemorySwapMax let the 320 MB allocation finish in 311 ms with 179 MB in zram swap, that is in RAM. `systemctl --user set-property --runtime <name>.slice MemoryHigh=.. MemoryMax=.. CPUWeight=..` gives a slice with no unit file its limits (drop-ins under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/systemd/user.control/), and a scope started with --slice=<name>.slice runs under them. The owner's direction (2026-11-06): Spawn's core is one agent that runs forever, is observable, and runs in provisioned resources, with local hot recovery; this objective is the provisioned resources.

Owner ruling (2026-11-06). The host has 31 GB of RAM, 31 GB of swap and 16 cores, and a 6 GB cap would kill ordinary cargo builds (the owner's panes peaked at 8.6-25.2 GB). Per execution and per gate: MemoryHigh 10G (throttled first), MemoryMax 12G, MemorySwapMax 4G, in place of task 96's MemoryMax 6G for an execution and 8G for a gate with no swap. Admission waits for room instead of starting. A gate killed by its memory limit is a host fault (objective 020's verdict): judged again after 020's host-fault backoff, never counted toward a halt, not an abort. The slice's totals (MemoryHigh 16G, MemoryMax 20G) have no ruling and stay; what they mean for admission with 12G envelopes is in (5). This objective's memory-limit kill, and objective 032's real one, are judged by the owner outside the sandbox (mission 7): the gate gets no delegated cgroup, so inside the gate's sandbox 029.sh exits 1 (never 2) on the base and on every candidate alike. Measured on this host on 2026-11-06 (systemd 262, kernel 7.3, python3 touching pages in 8 MiB steps in a transient scope) for the ruled shape: a process that grows page by page past MemoryHigh is throttled, not killed. Under MemoryHigh 80M and MemoryMax 96M it stalled at 80 MiB with no swap, and at 96 MiB with MemorySwapMax 16M (the swap filled first), and was still alive 60 s later; under 112M/128M/32M it stalled at 144 MiB; under 24M/32M/8M it took 46 s to reach 32 MiB and was still alive at 60 s. It reached MemoryMax and was killed only with MemoryHigh close below it: 92M/96M/16M in 2.7 s, 94M/96M/16M in 0.26 s, 30M/32M/8M in 7.8 s. The ruled 10G/12G has the 80/96 shape: a build that runs away grows page by page, pushes up to 4 GiB into zram and then crawls at about 10 GiB rather than dying at 12 GiB; the kill at MemoryMax comes to what gets there at once. Spawn does not stop a throttled execution (the owner made no ruling on one); it shows it (7).

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. Settings, all of them, with their defaults: SPAWN_ENVELOPE `systemd` (default) or `off`; SPAWN_SLICE `spawn.slice`; SPAWN_SLICE_MEMORY_HIGH 16G, SPAWN_SLICE_MEMORY_MAX 20G, SPAWN_SLICE_CPU_WEIGHT 50 (so Spawn yields to the host's other jobs, weight 100, under contention and uses idle CPU otherwise); SPAWN_EXECUTION_MEMORY_HIGH 10G, SPAWN_EXECUTION_MEMORY_MAX 12G and SPAWN_EXECUTION_MEMORY_SWAP_MAX 4G; SPAWN_GATE_MEMORY_HIGH 10G, SPAWN_GATE_MEMORY_MAX 12G and SPAWN_GATE_MEMORY_SWAP_MAX 4G (the owner's ruling). Sizes are bytes or a number with K, M, G or T (powers of 1024, as systemd reads them). A size that does not parse, the slice's MemoryHigh above its MemoryMax, an envelope's MemoryHigh above its own MemoryMax, or an envelope's MemoryMax above the slice's is an error at start (the loop and the integrator refuse to start and say which setting; each checks the slice and both envelopes, so a test that shrinks the slice sets every envelope), never a silent default. Every envelope caps its swap (4G by default), never leaves it unbounded: this host's swap is zram, RAM itself, and an envelope with unbounded swap bounds nothing (measured above); the slice caps no swap, so memory in zram is what admission's host measure (MemAvailable) sees.
2. The slice. When the loop starts with SPAWN_ENVELOPE=systemd and a reachable user manager that delegates the memory controller, it makes the slice carry its limits (`systemctl --user set-property --runtime`, or the D-Bus call; a unit file installed by deploy/ is as good for spawn.slice) before it starts any execution, and records `{"type": "host.envelope", "state": "systemd", "slice", "memory_high", "memory_max", "cpu_weight", "execution_memory_high", "execution_memory_max", "execution_memory_swap_max", "gate_memory_high", "gate_memory_max", "gate_memory_swap_max"}` (sizes in bytes) once, and again only when one of them changes (the latest read back from the log on start, as `host.disk` is). With no user manager reachable (no XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or no bus: the gate's sandbox empties /run), or one that does not delegate memory, executions and gates run as today and the loop records `{"type": "host.envelope", "state": "unavailable", "error"}` once (said once in its log); SPAWN_ENVELOPE=off runs as today and records `state` `off`. Every existing scenario runs in the gate's sandbox, so none of them may change. One slice per Spawn instance: the live fleet's is spawn.slice; a test or a second instance on the host names its own (029.sh: bb029_<run>.slice).
3. An execution's scope. Every execution, a start or a resume, whoever submitted it (the dispatcher, the liveness rule, the supervisor, a person), runs its engine in a transient scope `<slice stem>-<execution id>.scope` (spawn-exec_12.scope in spawn.slice) directly inside the slice, with MemoryHigh, MemoryMax and MemorySwapMax from the settings, OOMPolicy stop, and no unit left behind once its end is recorded, failed or not (--collect, or the unit's Result read and the unit then reset: a collected unit no longer says why it ended). The engine and everything it starts (builds, tests, tools and their children) are in that scope's cgroup. The runner (`spawn run`) may run inside the scope or outside it, so long as how the engine ended can be told (4). A loop restart or a deploy leaves running executions and their scopes as they are (KillMode=process today), and a restarted Bridge carries on with them as it does now.
4. A memory-limit kill ends that execution only. When the scope's limit kills a process (the kernel's OOM kill inside the scope: its memory.events oom_kill, or the unit's Result `oom-kill`), the whole execution ends (the engine and its children), its final checkpoint and its end run as for any end (no checkpointed work is lost, the workspace is not discarded), and objective 028 records it: `execution.interrupted` with cause `memory_limit`, path `resume` and evidence {"scope", "memory_max" (bytes), "oom_kills" (above 0), "memory_peak" (bytes, when it could be read)}; it is resumed by 028's rules (the same native session, after its bounded backoff, SPAWN_RECOVER_BACKOFF_SECS). Executions in other scopes, and the slice, are untouched.
5. Admission. An execution starts only when its envelope fits both under the slice and on the host:
- the slice: measured_bytes = the slice's memory that cannot be given back, `anon` + `shmem` of its memory.stat (anonymous and tmpfs memory stay in RAM or go to swap, which here is zram, RAM itself, and the host measure's to see; page cache is reclaimed under the limit and is not counted), threshold_bytes = the slice's MemoryMax minus the envelope's MemoryMax; it fits when measured_bytes <= threshold_bytes;
- the host: measured_bytes = MemAvailable of /proc/meminfo, threshold_bytes = the envelope's MemoryMax; it fits when measured_bytes >= threshold_bytes.
Otherwise the start or the resume waits: nothing starts, its command does not fail (it stays unfinished and is decided again at every pass, from the log, so a restarted loop goes on with it), and the wait is recorded once: `{"type": "admission.waiting", "kind": "execution", "agent_id", "session_id", "command_id", "envelope_bytes", "measure": "slice" | "host", "measured_bytes", "threshold_bytes"}` (the first measure that falls short, the slice first). When it starts after waiting: `{"type": "admission.admitted", "kind": "execution", "agent_id", "session_id", "command_id", "envelope_bytes", "waited_ms"}` (from the wait's first decision to the start, by the database's clock). A start that fits at once writes neither. The fleet view (`spawn fleet`, the dashboard's fleet) names an agent that waits for admission, with its measure and threshold. A gate: at each judging the integrator checks the same two measures for the gate's envelope, after objective 018's checks when 018 is solved (018's SPAWN_GATE_MIN_FREE_MEMORY_MB stays as it is); a gate that does not fit is not run this pass: `admission.waiting` with kind `gate` and `task` (no agent fields), which is not a verdict, moves no counter and keeps the task's place; it is checked again at the next pass, and `admission.admitted` (kind `gate`, `task`, `waited_ms`) is recorded when it runs after waiting. With the ruled defaults an execution and a gate have the same thresholds: the slice's anon + shmem at most 20 - 12 = 8 GiB (8.59 GB), MemAvailable at least 12 GiB (12.88 GB). What that means at today's load (the slice's totals stay, unruled; these numbers are for the owner): at 17:58 CST (09:58 UTC) on 2026-11-06 the 11 live executions held 117-260 MiB of anonymous memory each, 2.2 GiB together, and MemAvailable was 19.9 GiB, so today's fleet is admitted with 5.8 GiB of the slice's room and 7.9 GiB of the host's to spare. One gate at the integrator's measured peak (5.3 GB, 4.9 GiB, page cache included, so an upper bound) leaves under 1 GiB of the slice's room (2.2 + 4.9 = 7.1 GiB): beside it, a second gate, or any execution whose build holds more than about 0.9 GiB, holds every new start, resume and gate until one of them ends (admission stops nothing that runs). The owner's own work taking about 7.9 GiB more than now (the owner's panes peaked at 8.6-25.2 GB) puts MemAvailable under 12 GiB and holds all of Spawn's starts. The slice's MemoryHigh 16G throttles the whole slice once the fleet, one gate and one execution at its own MemoryHigh are together (2.2 + 4.9 + 10 = 17.1 GiB).
6. A gate's scope. The integrator runs each gate in a transient scope `<slice stem>-gate-<task id>-<n>.scope` directly inside the slice (n: that task's judging, from 1; a name is never reused while its unit exists), with SPAWN_GATE_MEMORY_HIGH, SPAWN_GATE_MEMORY_MAX and SPAWN_GATE_MEMORY_SWAP_MAX, OOMPolicy stop and no unit left behind (as in 3); everything the gate starts (bwrap, the builds, the scenarios and their engines) is in it, and its process group and wall-clock kill work as today. A gate its envelope kills (its scope's memory.events oom_kill above 0, or the unit's Result `oom-kill`, read at its end, never its exit status alone) is a host fault, not an abort (the owner's ruling): `task.gated` with objective 020's verdict `host_fault`, `evidence` `memory_limit`, `scope`, `memory_high`, `memory_max` (bytes), `oom_kills` and `memory_peak` (bytes, when it could be read), `reason` `host fault: the gate was killed by its memory limit (MemoryMax <size>, peak <size>), not a verdict, judged again later`, `log` (the gate's output) and 020's `host_faults`, `backoff_ms`, `due_ms` and `escalate`. The task stays where it was, its revisions do not move, nothing goes back to the worker, neither gate_rejections nor gate_aborts moves, and no halt rule counts it; no pass runs a gate for it before `due_ms` (SPAWN_GATE_HOST_FAULT_BACKOFF_SECS x 2^(k-1), at most an hour, read from the record), then it is judged again, in a scope of the next n. It shares 020's run of host faults (`gate_host_faults`) and its escalation at the second in a row. A gate killed past its wall clock, or ended by anything but its memory limit, is recorded as today. In the owner's order this objective comes after 020 (with 033) and uses its verdict (020 landed on main as e2c6976, task 94, after the deployed b950e25 these measures were taken on); solved first, it introduces `host_fault` as 020 describes.
7. Observable. `spawn fleet` and the dashboard's fleet show, for each live execution, its scope, its memory now, its peak, its MemoryHigh and MemoryMax, its swap and how often it was throttled (memory.current, memory.peak, memory.high, memory.max, memory.swap.current, memory.events `high`; bytes and a count), so an execution held at its MemoryHigh is seen, and the slice's (from `host.envelope` and the slice's cgroup).
8. Causality (§14): a kill is classified from the execution's own scope (its memory.events oom_kill or the unit's Result) read at its end and recorded with those facts, never from an exit code alone (137 is any SIGKILL) or from the host's state; an admission decision rests on the measures taken at that decision, recorded with their thresholds; the names of the slice and of each scope are in the records, so any reader finds the cgroup an execution or a gate ran in.

How the saving shows, in numbers (bytes and seconds). Spawn's memory is at most 20 GiB and throttled above 16 GiB, so at least 11 GiB of the 31.3 GiB stay the host's whatever Spawn runs; one execution or one gate is throttled above 10 GiB and holds at most 12 GiB of RAM and 4 GiB of zram swap (the gates' service peaked at 5.3 GB, an engine's peak was 0.28-4.7 GB with page cache, which a limit reclaims before it kills, the owner's builds 8.6-25.2 GB); today all of it is unbounded, plus 31.3 GiB of zram swap. A runaway allocation is confined to its envelope: killed when it reaches MemoryMax (130 ms from start to kill with a 64M cap and no MemoryHigh), throttled at MemoryHigh when it grows page by page (measured above); a kill costs one execution: work lost per memory-limit kill = what was written since its last checkpoint (checkpointed commits lost: 0), time to resume = 028's backoff plus a start (today a killed resident's engine is resumed 384-396 ms after its end; 029.sh allows 30 s from the record with a 1 s backoff); the sibling execution's uptime is unchanged (its oom_kill 0, the same execution). Under CPU contention Spawn's slice has half the weight of app.slice, where the owner's other jobs run, and all of an idle CPU otherwise. On 017's scorecard: reliability and autonomy no lower (no gate or execution killed by another's memory; a gate killed by its own is judged again, never an abort or a halt), cost and throughput unchanged at today's load.

State the rule in bridge.rs's module comment (the envelope, admission), in engine.rs, in gate.rs and integrate.rs's module comment (the gate's scope and its admission), in docs/design.md §11 (resources: the slice, the envelopes, admission), in docs/storage.md, and in deploy/systemd/README.md (the slice, and how to watch it: `systemctl --user status spawn.slice`, `systemd-cgtop`). Add unit tests: the sizes and the refusals at start; the scope names (the default slice, a named slice, a gate's); the admission decision (fits; the slice short; the host short; the slice checked first; the threshold arithmetic; one record per wait; admitted with waited_ms; a start that fits writes nothing); an end classified `memory_limit` from oom_kill or Result `oom-kill`, and not from exit 137 alone; `host.envelope` (systemd, unavailable, off) recorded once and read back; in crates/spawn-postgres/tests/: `spawn_host_record` (or the function that writes them) accepting `host.envelope`, `admission.waiting` and `admission.admitted`, and refusing them without their fields.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/029.sh (read it: its header lists today's measures). A real `spawn loop` (the Bridge, its pusher, the dispatcher, no supervisor, no model judge) runs three residents of one gated mission on a fake engine, each started by a task, in a slice of the run's own (bb029_<run>.slice, SPAWN_SLICE_MEMORY_HIGH=128M, SPAWN_SLICE_MEMORY_MAX=144M, the CPU weight at its default), with SPAWN_EXECUTION_MEMORY_HIGH=92M, SPAWN_EXECUTION_MEMORY_MAX=96M and SPAWN_EXECUTION_MEMORY_SWAP_MAX=16M, SPAWN_GATE_MEMORY_HIGH=30M, SPAWN_GATE_MEMORY_MAX=32M and SPAWN_GATE_MEMORY_SWAP_MAX=8M (every envelope set: the defaults do not fit under its slice; each MemoryHigh close below its MemoryMax, so that a page-by-page allocation reaches the kill, as measured above), SPAWN_GATE_HOST_FAULT_BACKOFF_SECS=3 and SPAWN_RECOVER_BACKOFF_SECS=1. Each engine notes, as it starts, its pid, its cgroup, that cgroup's memory.high, memory.max and memory.swap.max, a child's cgroup and whether work.txt is in its workspace. hog writes work.txt (checkpointed, pushed), then runs a tool (python3) that allocates past its envelope in 8 MiB steps up to 256 MiB, only under a memory.max of 256 MiB or less (uncapped it allocates nothing, so the host is never at risk); calm writes calm.txt and reports, then holds 56 MiB in a child while told to; late gets its task while calm holds. It checks:
- (1) hog's and calm's engines, and a child of each, run in bb029_<run>-<their execution id>.scope directly inside the slice, with memory.high 92 MiB, memory.max 96 MiB and memory.swap.max 16 MiB; the slice is active with memory.high 128 MiB, memory.max 144 MiB and cpu.weight 50; the loop's `host.envelope` record (state `systemd`) names the slice and every one of these settings in bytes;
- (2) the allocation is killed by the envelope: hog's execution ends within 20 s (its engine's pid gone), the slice's memory.events counts the OOM kill, and calm runs on (the same execution, its pid alive, its scope's oom_kill 0);
- (3) within 20 s an `execution.interrupted` record for hog's execution: cause `memory_limit`, path `resume`, evidence naming its scope, memory_max 100663296 and oom_kills above 0; within 30 s of it hog is resumed (its session, `--resume`) in a scope of its own in the slice, its workspace holding work.txt byte for byte; the killed execution's scope leaves no unit behind;
- (4) while calm holds 56 MiB (the slice's anon + shmem above 144 - 96 = 48 MiB), late does not start: within 20 s of its task's assignment an `admission.waiting` record (kind `execution`, measure `slice`, envelope_bytes 100663296, threshold_bytes 50331648, measured_bytes above it), and no engine of late starts while calm holds; once calm lets go, late's engine starts within 30 s in its own scope in the slice, after an `admission.admitted` record whose waited_ms covers the wait;
- (5) calm's reported task is judged by `spawn integrate --once` passes through a recording gate (SPAWN_GATE) that runs in bb029_<run>-gate-<task id>-<n>.scope inside the slice, with memory.high 30 MiB, memory.max 32 MiB and memory.swap.max 8 MiB, and on its first run allocates past that envelope (hog's tool);
- (6) that gate, killed by its memory limit, is a host fault: within 30 s a `task.gated` with verdict `host_fault`, `evidence` `memory_limit`, its scope, `memory_max` 33554432, `oom_kills` above 0, `backoff_ms` 3000 and `due_ms` its time + 3000; gate_aborts and gate_rejections unchanged, the task still `reported`, the mission not halted; no gate runs for it before `due_ms`; then it is judged again, in bb029_<run>-gate-<task id>-<a larger n>.scope, and accepted.
It needs a systemd user manager that delegates the memory controller, so it is judged outside the gate's sandbox: without one it exits 1 with "029: cannot be judged here: no systemd user manager is reachable (...)", never 2, so it never aborts a gate. It removes the units it made (its slice, the scopes in it, the slice's runtime drop-ins) and touches no other unit. On the live main (b950e25; the deployed binary is built from it) it fails at (1), in 2-17 s: "(1) hog's engine (execution exec_1, pid <pid>) runs in /user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/tmux-spawn-<uuid>.scope (memory.max max, memory.swap.max max), not in its own scope bb029_<run>-exec_1.scope inside bb029_<run>.slice: an execution has no envelope, and one allocation can take the host's memory". With BB_029_MEASURE=1 (only to show today's behaviour) it goes on (31-92 s): calm's engine and hog's are both in tmux's pane scopes with no limit, the slice is not active; uncapped, the tool allocates nothing, so the scenario kills hog's engine itself (SIGKILL to the pid it noted): the execution ends 1.38-1.42 s after the tool was told to run (the engine's 1 s poll included) and is recorded `execution.ended` cause `exited` with no exit code, no `execution.interrupted`; the residents' liveness rule resumes it 384-396 ms after its end, its own session, work.txt intact, again in a tmux scope; late starts 446-843 ms after its task's assignment with no admission record; the gate runs in the cgroup of the process that ran `spawn integrate`, with no limit; uncapped, its tool allocates nothing, so the measure's gate kills itself (SIGKILL), and today that is recorded `aborted` ("the gate failed: the gate ended with signal: 9 (SIGKILL)"; gate_aborts 0 -> 1, toward the halt after three) and the gate runs again 0.7 s later, at the next pass, with no due time (one measure run, 38.9 s, 2026-11-06 18:21 CST). It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails (or it cannot be judged on the host), 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: this objective cannot be judged by mission 4's gate, and the gate gets no delegated cgroup (the owner's ruling, 2026-11-06). Its scenario needs a systemd user manager and the gate's sandbox has none (its /run is empty by design: the user bus would let candidate code start units outside the sandbox), so inside the sandbox 029.sh exits 1 on the base and on every candidate alike, and no mission-4 candidate could pass it as its task scenario. It also needs the protected deploy/ (spawn.slice for the live fleet: its settings in spawn.env or a unit in deploy/systemd, deploy/systemd/README.md, and deploy.sh checking that the user manager delegates memory before it starts the loop). It is owner work: done in an owner task (mission 7), reviewed and merged by the owner, judged by the owner's run of 029.sh outside the sandbox (red on the base, green on the candidate) beside the gate's verdict on everything else, and deployed. Solve it with or after objective 028, whose `execution.interrupted` record (3) reads. Never weaken what the gate judges or hides (the sandbox, the protected list, the build-time checks, the test ratchet); add no build-time code; build offline from the cargo caches already on the host. None of the other objectives' scenarios may regress: every one of them runs where no user manager is reachable and must see today's behaviour. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and scripts/rsi/test-gate.sh passing, and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
